reason: Reproduced exactly, and it is the highest-value class this round names: an assertion that cannot fail for the finding it exists to hold. Driven in chromium at 390x844 with touch at ?v=light&state=full, getComputedStyle(.scroll) reads overflowX "clip", overflowY "visible", and scrollHeight === clientHeight === 2664 while document.scrollingElement is 2664/844. Per the overflow rules, visible is only coerced to auto when the other axis is neither visible NOR clip, so .scroll's overflow-y genuinely stays visible and .scroll is not a scroll container. I tapped the first .dot to pin the tip (before.on true, docTop 1170, .scroll.scrollTop 0), then ran the gate's exact line, document.querySelector(".scroll").scrollBy(0, 260): docTop stayed 1170 and .scroll.scrollTop stayed 0. after came back {on:true, drift:8} - the tip's resting 8px offset, measured over a page that never moved. So ok("a pinned label is dismissed or follows its mark", before && (!after.on || after.drift <= 24)) still guards that a tap pins and that the tip is placed near its mark, but the scroll leg - the whole r1 finding - is inert, and I confirmed no other assertion in the file covers it: the only other scroll drivers are the PageDown check at 1402-1408 (no tip involved) and a scrollWidth read at 1512. The behaviour underneath is sound - scrolling the document 260px for real kept the tip on and tracking at drift 8, and 1600px further dropped it once the mark left the viewport - which is what makes this a dead guard sitting over a working fix rather than a live bug. The stale model is written into the source too: the comment at lately.html:1176 still reads "The surface scrolls inside .scroll, not the document, so no scroll event reaches a window listener without capture", false since round 2 and contradicted by the CSS comment at 118 that says the document is the scroller. Line numbers are the one thing the seat got wrong and they are off by enough to matter for a fixer: the gate line is interaction-check.mjs:1206 not 1207, the CSS is lately.html:182 not 180, the CSS comment is 118 not 113, and the stale JS comment is 1176 not 1147 (1147 is inside the resize handler). The quoted text is verbatim and unambiguous in every case, so the finding stands; the fixer should use the corrected numbers. Severity defect is right and not overstated: nothing on screen is wrong today, so this is not misleading or blocking, but a guard that cannot fail plus a false mechanism recorded in the source is more than a refinement.
sharpenedFix: interaction-check.mjs:1206 - replace document.querySelector(".scroll").scrollBy(0, 260) with document.scrollingElement.scrollBy(0, 260), read document.scrollingElement.scrollTop immediately before and after, and add a separate ok() that the surface actually moved (moved > 0, not moved === 260, so the assertion does not false-fail if the mark ever lands near the document end and the scroll is short). Keep the drift assertion as it is; measured against the real document scroll it passes at drift 8 with on:true. Do not target .scroll defensively with a `|| document.scrollingElement` fallback - that is exactly the construction that let this rot silently; name the document scroller outright, and let the moved > 0 assertion be what fails if the scroller ever changes again. lately.html:1176 - rewrite the comment to say the document is the scroller (round 2), that a window scroll listener therefore does reach it, and that capture is kept defensively because there is no nested scroller on this surface today (I enumerated every element at 390/768/1440: zero elements compute overflow auto or scroll) but a scroll originating inside one would not bubble to window. There is no scroll-behavior: smooth anywhere in lately.html, so the existing 220ms wait after the scroll is still enough.
breaks: Nothing on the surface - the change is confined to the gate and one comment. Risks are in the gate itself: (1) the assertion becomes live for the first time, so re-run the full behaviour gate and confirm this block is still green (I measured it green: after a real 260px document scroll the tip stays on and tracks at drift 8). (2) The block's docTop after scrollIntoViewIfNeeded is 1170 of a 1820px maximum at 390x844 state=full, so 260px of headroom exists today; if the composition ever gets shorter at that width the new moved > 0 assertion is what catches it, which is the point, but whoever changes the vertical rhythm should expect this assertion to speak. (3) Re-measure nothing in audit.mjs - no CSS, token, type or contrast surface is touched. (4) After landing, grep the rest of interaction-check.mjs and lately.html for any other reference to .scroll as a scroller: line 1512 uses `document.querySelector(".scroll") || document.scrollingElement` and reads scrollWidth - clientWidth off it, which is 0 on a clip container, so the fortnight-label "nothing is clipped away inside the scroller" assertion is a candidate for the same rot and should be checked in the same pass.
